units.title: Culture and Land-Based Learning
units.summary: Connect design decisions to place, story, seasons, and respectful observation.
units.use: These activities help students notice context before deciding what to make.

lessons.title: Grandmother Moon, Seasons, and Turtle's Back
lessons.summary: Read seasonal patterns and use a turtle-shell model to organize observations.
lessons.use: Pattern, place, and careful observation support design and environmental learning.

lessons.title: Land Lettermark
lessons.summary: Build a lettermark from a place-based observation and document the design choice.
lessons.use: The activity connects visual identity, audience, and responsibility to place.

units.title: N.I.C.E. Design Process
units.summary: Move from a real situation to evidence, criteria, ideas, feedback, and revision.
units.use: The process makes design decisions explainable and repeatable in any project.

lessons.title: Understand the Situation
lessons.summary: Separate facts, assumptions, and interpretations before defining the problem.
lessons.use: A clear situation prevents a team from solving the wrong problem.

lessons.title: Record User Needs
lessons.summary: Observe and record what people actually need in the setting.
lessons.use: Evidence about users guides safer and more useful designs.

lessons.title: Necessities and Nice-to-Haves
lessons.summary: Separate non-negotiable constraints from preferences.
lessons.use: The distinction keeps safety and function visible when trade-offs appear.

lessons.title: Rank Priorities
lessons.summary: Rank preferences so the most valuable improvements stay visible.
lessons.use: Priorities help a team compare ideas without treating every wish as equal.

lessons.title: Investigate and Inquire
lessons.summary: Research, observe, measure, collect precedents, and generate several ideas.
lessons.use: Investigation replaces guesses with evidence and expands the possible solutions.

lessons.title: Create and Communicate
lessons.summary: Develop an idea, make the proposal understandable, pitch it, and collect feedback.
lessons.use: Clear communication lets other people test, question, and improve a proposal.

lessons.title: Evaluate and Repeat
lessons.summary: Score ideas against necessities and priorities, then revise the strongest option.
lessons.use: Evaluation turns feedback and test results into defensible improvements.

units.title: Logo Design in Photopea
units.summary: Learn browser-based graphic design by building a nameplate and logo in five short projects.
units.use: The sequence develops editable vector artwork for signs, labels, slides, and fabrication.

lessons.title: Build the Nameplate Text
lessons.summary: Make an 11 by 4 inch file, leave room for a logo, and choose readable type.
lessons.use: Correct size, spacing, and legibility prepare a design for real output.

lessons.title: Warm-Up: Trace the AA Logo
lessons.summary: Rebuild a simple hand-drawn mark with four clean vector lines.
lessons.use: The warm-up introduces editable vector shapes, visual checking, and SVG export.

lessons.title: Trace a Multi-Layer Logo
lessons.summary: Trace a landscape sketch as four named vector shapes and export an animation-ready SVG.
lessons.use: Separate layers make complex artwork easier to revise, colour, fabricate, and animate.

lessons.title: Combine Logo and Nameplate
lessons.summary: Combine the ANDRADE logo and nameplate, then export the complete design.
lessons.use: The worked example shows alignment, proportion, and file-export decisions.

lessons.title: Design Your Own Name Tag
lessons.summary: Apply the tutorial skills to an original name-and-logo design and defend the choices.
lessons.use: The project connects digital design, accessibility checks, and fabrication output.

units.title: Accessible Design
units.summary: Build accessibility checks into graphic design instead of adding them at the end.
units.use: Readable, well-described graphics work better on screens, in print, and on fabricated objects.

lessons.title: Access and Alt Text
lessons.summary: Describe the instructional purpose of an image and identify barriers to access.
lessons.use: Useful descriptions preserve meaning for people who cannot use the image visually.

lessons.title: Fonts and Text Effects
lessons.summary: Compare typefaces and test backgrounds, outlines, shadows, and decorative effects.
lessons.use: Legible type survives small screens, printing, engraving, and viewing from a distance.

lessons.title: Understanding Colour
lessons.summary: Use hue, saturation, value, opacity, and colour models deliberately.
lessons.use: Colour decisions affect emphasis, reproduction, and whether meaning survives greyscale.

lessons.title: Contrast and Output
lessons.summary: Check contrast, real size, file type, and final screen, print, or fabrication output.
lessons.use: Testing catches problems before a graphic is shared or made.

units.title: Laser Cutting and Fabrication Tools
units.summary: Use visual examples, measured drawings, builders, and reusable files to make laser-cut projects.
units.use: The tools support measured prototypes, shop organization, and iterative fabrication.

lessons.title: Make It Stand
lessons.summary: Compare ways to support a flat design as a stable object.
lessons.use: Support geometry is useful for signs, displays, holders, and models.

lessons.title: Measure and Place
lessons.summary: Measure a real object and place openings and supports from evidence.
lessons.use: Measured placement improves access, spacing, and fit.

lessons.title: Material Fit and Calibration
lessons.summary: Test material thickness, kerf, and fit before cutting a full project.
lessons.use: Calibration reduces wasted material and unreliable joints.

lessons.title: Assemblies and Hybrid Fabrication
lessons.summary: Combine cut parts, fasteners, and other processes into an assembly.
lessons.use: Hybrid fabrication expands what a flat-sheet process can make.

lessons.title: Wall and Bench Tool Module
lessons.summary: Design a visible, labelled, stable holder for a wall or workbench.
lessons.use: Good tool storage improves access, accountability, and shop safety.

lessons.title: Design and Fabrication Capstone
lessons.summary: Plan, prototype, test, and document an original fabricated solution.
lessons.use: The capstone combines evidence, design decisions, fabrication, and evaluation.

lessons.title: CNC Machining
lessons.summary: CNC machining resources are in development.
lessons.use: The future sequence will connect digital models to subtractive manufacturing.

lessons.title: 3D Printing
lessons.summary: 3D-printing resources are in development.
lessons.use: The future sequence will cover slicing, orientation, supports, and functional tolerances.

units.title: Orientation
units.summary: Learn how to use the notes, class materials, glossary, and submission links.
units.use: A clear starting routine makes independent work easier.

lessons.title: Course Orientation
lessons.summary: A concise orientation lesson is planned.
lessons.use: It will connect the site, classroom workflow, and project evidence.

units.title: Safety
units.summary: Recognize electrical, tool, data, and workspace hazards before beginning a task.
units.use: Safe habits protect people, equipment, and project evidence.

lessons.title: Technology Lab Safety
lessons.summary: The consolidated safety lesson is planned.
lessons.use: It will connect hazard recognition to classroom procedures.

units.title: Design
units.summary: Use the N.I.C.E. process to define needs, develop ideas, and evaluate evidence.
units.use: Design reasoning supports circuits, computing, fabrication, and control projects.

lessons.title: N.I.C.E. Design Process
lessons.summary: Use the General Design & Fabrication learning path.
lessons.use: The shared process prevents duplicate design notes.

units.title: Project Portfolio
units.summary: Collect plans, tests, code, measurements, photographs, and reflections.
units.use: A portfolio shows both the result and the engineering process that produced it.

lessons.title: Build a Technical Portfolio
lessons.summary: The portfolio lesson is planned.
lessons.use: It will support class assessment and future applications.

units.title: Circuits and Electronics
units.summary: Move from measurement and notation to progressively harder circuit analysis packages.
units.use: These methods explain power paths in computers, vehicles, robots, sensors, and control systems.

lessons.title: Series Circuits
lessons.summary: Calculate current, voltage drops, resistance, and power in one-path circuits.
lessons.use: Series rules appear in sensor chains, voltage drops, and component strings.

lessons.title: Parallel Circuits
lessons.summary: Calculate branch currents, common voltage, equivalent resistance, and power.
lessons.use: Parallel paths keep loads operating independently in buildings, vehicles, and computers.

lessons.title: Series-Parallel Circuits
lessons.summary: Reduce mixed networks in stages and verify currents and voltages.
lessons.use: Real systems often combine shared paths with parallel loads.

lessons.title: Kirchhoff's Laws
lessons.summary: Write current and voltage equations for circuits that cannot be reduced directly.
lessons.use: Kirchhoff analysis supports troubleshooting and more advanced network methods.

lessons.title: Linear Algebra for Circuits
lessons.summary: Solve simultaneous circuit equations by substitution, elimination, and matrices.
lessons.use: The method prepares students for college and university network analysis.

units.title: Computer Systems
units.summary: Connect components, power, firmware, storage, operating systems, and recovery as one system.
units.use: System thinking supports repair, commissioning, and reliable computing projects.

lessons.title: Computer Systems Sequence
lessons.summary: The current computer-systems notes remain available while their package order is reconciled.
lessons.use: The final sequence will connect hardware evidence to recovery and commissioning.

units.title: Linux and Operating Systems
units.summary: Choose, install, explore, administer, program, and measure a Linux computer in a linear sequence.
units.use: Linux skills support repair, servers, embedded systems, networking, automation, and engineering tools.

lessons.title: Choosing a Linux Distribution
lessons.summary: Compare distribution families, desktop environments, hardware needs, software, and support.
lessons.use: A good choice matches the computer and the work instead of following a brand name.

lessons.title: Install Linux Mint
lessons.summary: Prepare installation media, protect data, install Mint, and verify the result.
lessons.use: The procedure supports computer recovery and prepares a system for later projects.

lessons.title: Explore Linux
lessons.summary: Explore the desktop, accounts, files, terminal, and Bashcrawl while collecting evidence.
lessons.use: The activity builds confidence before students administer or program the system.

lessons.title: Know Your Linux Computer
lessons.summary: Record hardware, operating-system, storage, and device information.
lessons.use: A verified inventory supports troubleshooting, upgrades, and performance comparisons.

lessons.title: Files, Terminal, and Permissions
lessons.summary: Navigate paths, inspect files, and use permissions safely.
lessons.use: These skills are essential for administration, automation, and development.

lessons.title: Git Version Control
lessons.summary: Record, inspect, and share changes with a safe Git workflow.
lessons.use: Version control protects project history and supports collaboration.

lessons.title: Build a Quarto Website
lessons.summary: Turn Markdown, code, and media into a small technical website.
lessons.use: A website makes project evidence and explanations easy to review and share.

lessons.title: Publish with GitHub Pages
lessons.summary: Publish a reviewed static site without exposing secrets or private files.
lessons.use: Deployment turns local documentation into a durable public portfolio.

lessons.title: Python Measurement Logging
lessons.summary: Write a small Python program that records measurements with units and timestamps.
lessons.use: Logging supports sensor tests, performance studies, and repeatable experiments.

lessons.title: Python Analysis and Curve Fitting
lessons.summary: Inspect recorded data and fit a simple model.
lessons.use: Analysis connects observations to engineering decisions and predictions.

lessons.title: Networking, SSH, and tmux
lessons.summary: Diagnose a network connection and manage a remote Linux session safely.
lessons.use: Remote administration is common for servers, Raspberry Pi systems, and lab equipment.

lessons.title: Power and Raspberry Pi Bridge
lessons.summary: Connect computer power concepts to a future Raspberry Pi build without inventing a lab.
lessons.use: The calculation bridge prepares students to reason about supplies, loads, and interfaces.

units.title: Networking
units.summary: Move from local addressing and diagnosis to secure remote access.
units.use: Networks connect computers, controllers, sensors, and services.

lessons.title: Networking Sequence
lessons.summary: Core networking appears in the Linux path while a dedicated module is developed.
lessons.use: The future module will add switching, routing, and service design.

units.title: Programming and Interfacing

units.title: Robotics and Control Systems

units.use: Control systems appear in robots, vehicles, manufacturing, and buildings.

units.use: The track prepares students for formal problem solving in circuits, data, energy, and systems.
